title: Supreme Court keeps injunction against DEI grant defunding in place
gist: The Supreme Court declined, without comment or dissent, to hear the government's appeal of an injunction restoring DEI-related grants to seven University of California researchers, leaving in place an appeals ruling that canceling individual grants for their viewpoint violates the First Amendment — a signal other courts may read as the Trump administration's anti-DEI grant purge being on shaky legal ground.

themes.theme: Supreme Court declines DEI grant appeal

insights.claim: The Supreme Court refused, with no discussion and no dissents, to hear an appeal of a ruling blocking the government from canceling grants of seven University of California researchers terminated under the Trump administration's anti-DEI purge.
insights.speaker: John Timmer
insights.so_what: Leaves a First Amendment precedent against viewpoint-based grant cancellation standing.

insights.claim: The Supreme Court's decision not to intervene may be read by other courts as a sign that the government's anti-DEI grant terminations are on shaky legal ground.
insights.speaker: John Timmer

insights.claim: An appeals court held the government may eliminate entire grant programs but canceling individual grants it disagrees with is viewpoint discrimination and an attempt at 'suppression of dangerous ideas', violating the First Amendment.
